differences.what: Massing: three storeys over a raised basement at the photograph's heights (principal floor 1.65 m, the projection's top 9.45 m, the wall head 12.45 m) — the draft's were the rules' (T-2543)

Gable: the front carried up as a shaped Flemish gable over the whole front, swelling from a kneeler each side and drawn in to a pointed head under a finial at 17.0-17.5 m, in place of the draft's stepped boxes (T-2543)

Gable: the outline re-read on both sides at a tenth of a metre and redrawn: the swell a convex curve from 2.98 m out at 13.0 m to 1.83 at 14.5 m swinging in to the shoulders, where the draft stood 0.3-0.5 m wide of it, and the head a bell from 1.10 m at 15.3 m to 0.35 at 16.5 m on the finial's square plinth (0.48 m across from 16.65 m), which the draft drew as a point; the print's south side reads about 0.25 m wider than its north all the way up and the build takes the mean (T-2951)
Gable: the grid window nine lights, three rows of three about 0.44 by 0.37 m between stone mullions and over stone transoms, in the 1.64 by 1.26 m opening (T-2951)

Gable: its face on the wall's own plane, as the print's: the eave under it plain and 0.05 m deep, so the slab stands 0.07 m before the wall below, its foot just over the third storey's arches, with no eave, fascia or gutter across the front (T-2889)

Gable: each kneeler a carved scroll console at the front's corner (its roll from about 11.35 m, its body up to a cap under the slab's foot) under a small pinnacle on the ledge 3.85 m out, where the draft stood a plain square pinnacle (T-2951)
Gable: the shoulder stones square blocks 0.9-1.62 m out from 14.6 to 15.22 m, standing over the outline through the slab (T-2951)
Gable: each shoulder stone carries a sunk panel about 0.26 by 0.11 m near its top, the print's slot of shadow; built so, 0.04 m sunk in the block's face (T-3090)

Gable: the grid window stands in quoined side stones (about 0.34 m, one a row each side, long and short in turn) under a moulded hood just over its head whose upper edge waves up to a crown at the middle and flicks up at each end (y 245-250 px), over a deep two-step moulded shelf about 1.8 m across from 13.05 to 13.33 m (y 370-395 px); built so, K06's own sill gone (T-3090)

Gable: the grid window's lights read as dark openings between the stone mullions and transoms; built with no K06 sash, a dark backing behind glass in a thin frame at the recess's back, where K06's casement frame read heavier (T-3090)

Gable: the kneelers' scrolls are carved, a rosette in each roll's eye; built so, eight petals round a boss. The carved block under each scroll in the print, down the front's corner, is the rainwater pipe's head (the downpipes' T-2953 item), not the console's (T-3090)
South projection: carried through the basement and two storeys to a flat top at the third floor, with the round-arched window, the basement light and the paired window in it (T-2543)

South projection: flush with the south corner, as the print's, its south cheek running on in the side wall's plane, and its north face kept on the print's (5.05 m out, the projection 5.05 m across where K08 had stood it 0.3 m in) (T-2953)

South projection: the barred basement light from the print's walk line up, over a 0.1 m plinth, the light 0.86 m clear to its head at 1.08 m, where K08 had kept it 0.65 m high over the 0.6 m plinth (T-2953)
Balcony: the iron balcony on the projection's top, round its cheeks and front, its rail about 0.5 m over the cornice as the print's (47 px both) and its balusters 0.24 m apart (T-2888)

Balcony: the middle of its front run (x 390-680 px) is a solid stone panel rising to a central pedestal (x 527-557 px), with iron scrolls against it and roundels on the balusters either side; built so, the panel 3.14 m across, 0.09 m high at its ends and swept straight up over 0.8 m to 0.42 m shoulders, the pedestal 0.32 m across and 0.52 m high under a cap at about the rail's top, an iron scroll hung from the rail over each sweep, a carved scroll beside the pedestal each side, and a roundel under the rail on every baluster. The print's iron scrolls are larger (about 0.11 m against 0.07) and stand before the panel's slope where the build's hang clear of it in the rail's plane (T-3113; L-k08-1812-balcony-panel-3113)

South projection: its top brought down to the print's cornice, the foot at about y 700 px and the top at y 677-693 (the print is warped, lower to the north): the last storey 3.65 m, the wall head at 9.25 m under an eave 0.2 m out and 0.15 m deep to 9.40 m, where K08's 0.28 m fascia over the 9.45 m wall head had stood about 25-30 px over the print's, and the balcony stands on it at the print's height; the render's top reads at about y 679 (T-3113; L-k08-1812-balcony-panel-3113)

South projection: under the cornice the print's face is a stone frieze from the cornice's foot down to the paired window's caps (y 700-740 px, about 8.8-9.25 m), with a block under the balcony's pedestal (x 527-557) and a moulded band at the caps' top; built as brick, the cornice's section as a plain soffit and fascia where the print's is moulded (T-3113)

Third storey: the large window over the balcony under its flat segmental arch (2.78 m across, crown 12.05 m) with its fanlight, and the small round-arched window to its north (1.2 m, crown 12.0 m), each in a ring of voussoirs running up into the gable's face, the large one under its keystone (T-2889)
Second storey: the north window one wide window, 1.64 m across on a stone mullion, under a transom (T-2889)

Third storey: the large window's middle light is wider than the two beside it (about 120 px against 40-43, between posts about 0.2 m) and carries a low moulded arch of its own whose crown stands about 0.16 m over the side lights' transoms; heavy bars run on from the posts' heads to the head, and the fanlight has a concentric bar about 0.25 m inside its glass as well as radial ones; built so, lights 1 : 2.9 : 1, the middle arch from the posts' heads, the post bars leaning 23 degrees out and the concentric bar over eleven radial ones. The print's middle arch springs from the posts lower than the side transoms, where the build's springs on the transom bar (T-3091; L-k01-1812-wheeler-windows-3091)

Third storey: the small arched window is filled with a patterned light, a border of small round panes round a figured field, set deep; built as a leaded light, a came round the field 0.12 m in, the border cut into short panes, diamond quarries and a roundel in the field standing for the figure, in a 0.2 m reveal. The figure itself is not modelled (T-3091; L-k01-1812-wheeler-windows-3091)

Third storey: the voussoirs alternate long and short into the brick; built so on both arches, the short stones 0.28 and 0.26 m where the long are the rings' 0.43 and 0.40 m, the keystone's neighbours short. The stones' stepped ends are cut on the ring's radii, not squared to the brick courses (T-3091; L-k01-1812-wheeler-windows-3091)
Second storey: the north window's transom lights are glazed in small squares; built as eight by eight lights about 0.05 m square on muntins over one glass (T-3091; L-k01-1812-wheeler-windows-3091)

Gable: from the kneelers (about 11.6-11.7 m) to the ledge (12.55 m) the print's outline is already drawing in, about 3.98 m out on its south side over the scroll (x 344-365 px), where the slab's base ran out square 4.47 m past the side walls; built drawn in from the slab's foot to 4.0 m out at the ledge, the kneeler pinnacles' outer faces (T-3090)

Entrance: the porch's broad arch, a segment 2.7 m across rising 0.79 m from its spring (4.28 m over the walk) to its crown (5.07 m; its ring's top 5.22 m), the transom at its spring and the segment over it glazed in three lights; under it the double door, a 0.29 m pier and the side light, 1.04 m across from a sill 0.56 m over the floor (T-2952)

Stair: the straight stair to the walk between solid stone cheeks, level 0.5 m over the landing and swept down to a block 1.1 m high at the foot, the landing run on north as a terrace behind a stone parapet pierced in two rows of square holes, the print's pierced panel at the landing (T-2952)

Entrance: the arch's south jamb and moulding run down the projection's north corner in the print (its outer moulding at about x 740-755 px), so the arch reads about 0.3 m further south and broader; the build stands its 2.7 m mouth clear of the projection, from 5.2 m

Entrance: the arch is turned in a narrow moulded ring of light stone, and its curve is flatter at the crown than a segment (nearer a half ellipse); built as K01's voussoir block on a segmental head with a keystone flush with the ring

Entrance: the transom under the fanlight is a heavy moulded beam about 0.25 m deep, and the fanlight's three lights are divided by narrow columns of small panes; built as K07's 0.07 m bar and three plain lights
Stair: the north cheek flares out as it sweeps down and both end in a carved newel under a cap; built straight, to a plain block

Fabric: a rock-faced stone basement to a smooth water table, the entrance bay's first storey in coursed stone up to the second floor's belt, and brick over it, banded and dressed in stone (the belts, sills, flat arches, voussoirs, the north window's quoined surround); the south projection brick over its rock-faced basement, its bands, sills, heads and reveals stone (T-2914)

Fabric: over the second storey's north window, from the projection's north face to the corner, the carved frieze (8.55-8.95 m) under a moulded band and the patterned band of sunk panels (9.15-9.63 m) under a ledge, and the carved bosses under the projection's second-storey jambs (T-2915)
Fabric: the projection's windows in quoined stone jambs, short and long in turn, and the band at the arched window's spring running from each corner to the arch (T-2915)
Carving: the frieze is an interlace of crossing straps and leaves and the bosses carved shields; built as T-2819's guilloche of rings and plain oval bosses in a moulded ring

South projection: the second storey's jamb stones rise past the window's head to small carved caps under the projection's cornice (8.53-8.80 m), its mullion is a heavy pier (0.24 m) carried up as far, a moulded hood stands over the sashes' heads (8.04 m) and over it a low transom light in each bay glazed in small squares to 8.64 m; built so, the quoins carried to 8.53 m under dressed caps whose carving (a swag) is a raised oval boss (T-3091; L-k01-1812-wheeler-windows-3091)
Tone: the print's stone reads lighter than its brick; the built brown sandstone renders darker than the buff brick beside it (the colours are not shown, the relation is)

Downpipes down both ends of the front: the north one from a head under the north kneeler (10.3 m, the print's pipe top) down the main front's north end to grade; the south one down the projection's south corner from a head under its cornice to grade, and from a head under the south kneeler down the main front to the projection's top (T-2953)

Roof: a mansard behind the gable, in place of K01's 45-degree hip: straight steep slate faces (72 degrees, the north corner's lean, about 0.5 m out over 1.6 m of rise) from the side walls' heads at 12.45 m to a level curb at 14.45 m, the upper hip over it at 10 degrees and out of sight, so each shoulder shows a slate face laid in level courses under a level top; the north top renders at y 294-296 px against the print's cap at 302-313 (T-3033)

Roof: at the south the print's slate face ends in a vertical band (x 277-293 px) standing just outside the south wall's line, from the slate's foot up to a heavier level cap at y 257-277 px, about 0.4 m over the north cap, with the tall stack standing on it: the south wall carried up past the curb as a coped parapet (the c. 1955 photograph sees the same coped top from the south, T-3034). T-3061: built so, K01's mansard side parapet, the wall's own 0.33 m from the rear wall to the front, its 0.2 m coping's top at 14.5 m, the print's cap (rendered at y 267-282); the slate face behind it dies into its inner side. Its end renders at x 320-350, the wall line's offset (below)

South stack: Levy's shaft (x 262-318 px, top y 127) and the c. 1955 photograph's place it 1.35-2.35 m behind the main front, standing outside the south wall's line, topping 16.8 m; moved there from 6.1 m back at 17.59 m (T-3034), and T-3061 stands it on the south wall's outer face (v -0.55 to 0), carried to the ground as an outside breast, where it rendered about 60 px north of the print's on the wall line: its shaft now renders at x 288-345, 26-27 px north of the print's, the wall line's offset (below; L-k01-1812-wheeler-parapet-3061)

South wall line: the print's main front's south corner (its downpipe at x 293-300 px) stands about 23 px south of the build's (x 320), and the parapet's end and the outside stack by the same 26-30 px, about 0.26-0.31 m: sheet 28's traced wall may lie that far inside the wall the print shows (the permit's 30 ft, 9.14 m, is wider than the traced 8.5 m); the footprint is not moved for one reading (T-3075)
Colour: the print is monochrome, so every stone, brick and paint colour
The side and rear walls, which the photograph does not see
